source: https://api.explainingmarkets.ai/v1/archive (production competition API, official historical archive endpoint)
retrieval_method: GET /v1/archive manifest, then direct download of each sealed file's short-lived CloudFront-signed url, size-verified byte-for-byte against the manifest's reported bytes
selection_rule: Only quarters with sealed=true were downloaded. 2026Q3 (sealed=false, still being finalized as of retrieval) was deliberately excluded.
validation_performed: byte-for-byte size match against manifest for every downloaded file
zero duplicate event_id within any single file
zero duplicate event_id across all files combined (6287 unique / 6287 total)
event_datetime is monotonically non-decreasing within every file and across the combined, quarter-ordered load
knowledge_cutoff < event_datetime for every one of the 6287 records (0 violations)
car1 present only when return_status == "ok" (1 of 6287 records is status="closed"/return_status=None and correctly excluded from the label set)
earnings_surprise present only when surprise_status == "ok" (6145 ok, 141 missing_eps, 1 none)
known_limitations: disclosure.generated_at postdates event_datetime by months in most records (batch backfill), so it should not be read as 'shortly after the call' - only the disclosure CONTENT (derived solely from that event's own transcript) is treated as point-in-time-safe, never the generation timestamp.

earnings_surprise carries no separate consensus-estimate timestamp; it is computed in the same post-hoc batch as event_returns (see returns_computed_at on individual records) and is therefore treated strictly as a realized, post-event label/benchmark, never as a feature - per this dataset's own evidence, not assumption.
All 6,287 events currently on file are single-focal-asset EARNINGS_RELEASE events; no multi-asset event has been observed in this download.
